title: Phase 8: Convex platform and VTT
definitionOfDone: A PBI is done when every acceptance criterion is proved (DONE with non-empty proof) and at least one of its journey tests, verified to drive the real flow, passes. After each PBI, run that feature's regression suite plus the suites of the features that depend on it. PERF runs at feature completion and at release. The final pre-staging run (yarn validate:pre-staging:local on one source state) is the release-candidate check. A PBI that adds no user-visible flow (a refactor, removal, internal typing, documentation or measurement) sets journeyStatus internal with an internalReason, and is done when every criterion is proved; real play is checked by UAT (user, 2026-10-29).

ac.IN_PROGRESS: Started, or proved in part; some proof is still missing.

pbi.IN_PROGRESS: Some criteria started or done, or all done without proof or without a verified journey test.
pbi.DONE: Every criterion DONE with proof and journeyStatus verified.

journeyStatus.verified: The listed journey tests drive the whole user-visible flow through real code (convex-test, the real Session room, Playwright or session-worker native tests).
journeyStatus.partial: The journey tests cover part of the flow; journeyGap says what is missing.
journeyStatus.none: No journey test exists for the flow.
journeyStatus.internal: The PBI adds no user-visible flow (refactor, removal, typing, docs or measurement); internalReason says why, and its criteria proofs are the evidence.

uat.NOT_RUN: Not run on the rebaselined ledger.

features.title: Accounts
features.summary: Signup, login, password reset, usernames, profile privacy, superadmin authorization and account deletion.

pbis.title: Sign in works on web and native

acs.text: Authenticated SSR renders, hydrates and reloads with an HttpOnly/Lax session cookie in a real browser against personal dev.
Native-compatible bearer/JWT calls succeed, and sign-out, revoked JWTs and unauthenticated protected routes are denied or redirected.
The authenticated shell sends no legacy tRPC or Supabase request, and disposable accounts are cleaned up exactly.
Early typing survives blocked hydration, premature submission is blocked and fragment cleanup completes without warnings.

pbis.title: Signup stays closed unless the server opens it

acs.text: An unset signup flag reports signup as disabled.
Real Better Auth email/password signup is rejected with EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED, with no test bypass.

proof: apps/apis/convex/accountJourneys.test.ts › signs up, verifies the emailed link, logs in by email and username, reads with a native bearer JWT and signs out
acs.note: The repo proof drives the real Better Auth HTTP handler in-process (convex-test), not over a local socket; the real-local-HTTP run is the historical .codex evidence.

acs.text: A verified account makes protected native bearer/JWT reads; recovery and revocation work and signup bypass is denied.
proof: apps/apis/convex/accountJourneys.test.ts › signs up, verifies the emailed link, logs in by email and username, reads with a native bearer JWT and signs out

acs.text: The /auth/confirmed callback and rendered local delivery pass the current-source auth and email tests (16/16).

pbis.title: Invite someone to create an account

acs.text: Invitations are issued only through the internal CLI, with hashed, recipient-bound 256-bit tokens that expire and rotate.
Redemption atomically creates an ordinary account and consumes the token; invalid, expired, wrong-recipient, replayed and username-colliding redemptions fail and late failures roll back.
Deployed HTTP keeps the issuer and redeemer private and denies foreign origins.
Concurrent redemption on personal dev succeeds exactly once per fixture, followed by login and bearer-protected calls, with signup still closed.

pbis.title: Log in

acs.text: Email or username login returns to the requested path with account isolation, SSR/reload, an HttpOnly/Lax cookie, sign-out, and revoked-JWT and protected-route denial.
Overlapping session-convergence invalidation no longer blanks the home route, and regression tests prove eventual convergence and revocation behavior.
The two-account login/profile browser journey and the original Feat browser reproduction pass on unchanged source with exact cleanup.

pbis.title: Reset a forgotten password

acs.text: Password recovery is atomic, with resend and exhaustion limits and safe concurrent resets.
Wrong and consumed codes and password mismatches are rejected, and the reset URL carries no secret across reload.
A reset denies the old password and existing JWTs, isolates a second account and allows a new login with SSR and logout.

pbis.title: Choose a username

acs.text: Usernames are normalized, moderated and unique, with Better Auth as the uniqueness authority and availability checks advisory only.
In the browser, a colliding username is rejected, and rename, case-only display preservation, reload and login with the new canonical username pass.
The profile uses the real Convex subscription hook, receiving updates and unsubscribing on auth loss.

Username moderation is tiered (Q22): normalized names are split into parts at separators, case changes and letter-digit changes; a blocked part, an unambiguous term anywhere, or a blocked word plus dictionary words (server-side) is refused; ordinary names such as Cassandra, Classic, Dickens, Essex, Glasshouse and Assassin are accepted; ass_muncher, AssMuncher, Ass1Muncher and assmuncher are refused.

apps/apis/convex/usernameModeration.test.ts through the real auth.handler: refused at sign-up and rename, never at sign-in

pbis.title: Control who sees my profile

acs.text: Profile query and update act only on the caller; real native requests deny anonymous access and extra or spoofed user IDs.
A two-account browser journey that reuses the same browser storage leaks neither bio nor username.
Profile components handle the real subscription hook, auth loss, draft isolation and unsaved or in-flight edits (12 component tests).

The owner sets their profile to Private (the default) or Public. Private: only the owner can read it. Public: any signed-in account can open the owner's profile page and see its public fields (username, avatar and bio; account details such as email stay owner-only). Switching back to Private removes access at once, and a two-account journey proves what the other account sees under each setting. The minimal identity shown on Social listings and applications is unchanged.
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-12 from Q4: owner-only by default, plus a public/private setting like most social apps. Which fields are public is decided at implementation from the profile DTO and recorded in the decisions doc. Done 2026-10-12 by lane 2 (127e99cd4, 591d6b138; D109): username, bio and avatar are public; unknown, banned and private targets return the same null; a timed ban hides the profile only until banExpires. The two-account proof runs the real Convex queries; the live browser journey (profile-browser in tests/live-backend/authenticatedSession.ts) runs with lane 2's live batch.

pbis.title: Superadmin-only actions

acs.text: Role provisioning is internal-only, UUID-targeted and requires a verified active target.
Authorization reads the live stored role and session, rejects bans, revocation and ordinary users, and has no second role authority.
Every provider-admin endpoint, including impersonation and arbitrary user updates, returns 404.
Social moderation list, open and review operations use the shared superadmin guard.

pbis.title: Control who can edit and use content

pbis.title: Creature AC is computed from what it wears and holds
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-10 by the product owner (D107). Introduces the hand slots (MAIN_HAND, OFF_HAND, CARRIED, WORN) and the shared hand-occupancy function that SHEET-8, ATTACK-18 and ATTACK-19 reuse. D&D Beyond keeps a fixed AC with a note; computed AC is deliberate.

acs.text: A Creature's authored loadout places each item in the main hand, off hand, carried or worn, with at most one item per hand and a two-handed weapon blocking the off hand; an Encounter instance copies the loadout, and the GM can change it for that instance.
acs.note: Slice A (T1) done 2026-10-11: useState is MAIN_HAND | OFF_HAND | CARRIED | WORN; publication and the instance replacement refuse a two-handed item in or blocking the off hand (red-first proof with both checks neutralized); SRD Creatures get deterministic hands; Disarm moves an item from either hand. T4 done 2026-10-11: the editor test sets Off hand and the natural armor bonus and submits them; the journey copies the SRD Goblin, publishes, and refuses a two-handed main-hand item beside the shield.

acs.text: Every Creature's AC is computed like a Character's: worn armor with its Dex cap (or 10 + Dex unarmored), plus one held shield with its magic bonus, plus an authored natural armor bonus, plus modifiers. There is no fixed AC or AC note, and giving an instance a +1 shield or dropping its shield changes its AC.
acs.note: Slice B (T2) done 2026-10-11: armorClass and armorClassNote are removed for a required naturalArmorBonus; resolveDnd5eCreatureArmorClass shares the Character formula and counts a shield only in a hand. Encounter projection, cleaving, companions and the Creature detail read use it; a +1 shield replacement raises an instance's AC and a won Disarm of its shield lowers it. Equipment whose AC modifier is not the while-equipped form is refused at publication, Encounter admission and loadout replacement; the detail read shows no AC instead of failing. T4 done 2026-10-11: editing the Goblin (shield carried, natural armor 1) takes a new Run from 15 to 14 once the Blueprint is updated, while a Run already created keeps its pinned 15. A replacement's AC evaluability is checked per item by pinCreatureEquipmentSources (the redundant whole-loadout check is deleted), and the refusal test asserts the room-logged cause.

acs.text: Every SRD Creature is re-authored so its computed AC equals its printed AC (a wolf is 10 + 2 Dex + 1 natural = 13; the goblin holds a scimitar and a shield, carries a shortbow and wears leather armor); a conditional AC such as "12 (15 with mage armor)" authors the base value. A source-data test proves every one.
acs.note: Done 2026-10-11: all 317 SRD Creatures compute their printed AC. The oracle is SRD_CREATURE_STAT_BLOCKS in packages/source-data (generated from the SRD PDF), not SRD_CC_v5.1.txt. Conditional ACs author the base (archmage, mage, druid, dryad and the lycanthropes 0; ankheg 4); armor the SRD Equipment lacks is natural armor (skeleton 1, warhorse skeleton 2, frost giant 6).

features.title: Rules engine
features.summary: The node runtime and Rules Kernel that execute authored rules, pause and resume them.

pbis.title: Run authored rules, pause and resume them

acs.text: The node runtime uses one neutral resolver and normalizer with current System, source, ownership, bounds and checksum validation.
Assisted START persists a sealed pause without exposing partial Run state, resumes through a second pause and settles initiative and receipts atomically.
Resume admits only the exact System, executes frozen and source-independent, and rejects tampered or invalid evidence (26 runtime tests).
Stored bindings, private player reads and terminal replay are covered.
Mixed dice-plus-modifier healing keeps its roll identity through the kernel.
acs.note: SRD Potion of Healing: rolls the authored 2d4, adds the resolved modifier once, refuses a resolved expression with other dice.

acs.text: Multiple damage parts on one path keep their identity through the kernel.
acs.note: SRD Adult Red Dragon Bite: rolls, totals and types each part separately; refuses swapped and duplicate outcome identities.

features.title: Character Builder
features.summary: Character drafts, Builder choices and commit, and reconciliation when sources change.

pbis.title: Save Character drafts

acs.text: Character drafts support create/reopen, save, UUID/alias reads, private paginated recovery and discard.
Generation and active-baseline guards reject stale writes, System binding is immutable, quotas count drafts and Characters together, and Sheet-owned state is preserved.
Web bindings cover a stable create retry, save, recovery and a visible generation-bound Discard draft action.

pbis.title: Build a Character from choices and commit it

acs.text: Fighter/Rogue multiclass, Life Cleric preparation and slot use, and choice-heavy Dragonborn Builder-to-Sheet journeys pass serially with clean browser diagnostics.
Commit checks the server draft baseline and generation, requires readiness, materializes starting equipment only on first activation, and atomically persists the Character and consumes the draft.

Builder resolution stays within Convex limits with full dynamic validation, and native completions show only expected authentication negatives. Builder evaluation runs in the browser over content snapshots with 0 Convex calls per edit, autosave of 32 KB or less, commit database I/O of 450 KB or less for one Class plus 200 KB for each further distinct Class (D84), a full build of 1.5 MB or less, and a Builder worker chunk of 300 KB gzipped or less (ADR 0036).

pbis.title: Characters reconcile when sources change

acs.text: Builder preview and commit reconcile current publications through the removal-only rules runtime while preserving Sheet state.
Repair rows keep identity, history and private state, block Sheet play until ready and return to ACTIVE only through a ready commit.
After a same-source publication replacement, read-only preview removes an invalid chosen grant and commit repairs it while keeping UUID, route, damaged HP and inventory.
Direct unshare, authored deletion, membership departure and assignment replacement reconcile personal, assigned and create-only state with containing-transaction rollback.

pbis.title: Imported custom items keep their kind, properties and damage
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-11 by the product owner; done 2026-10-11. D&D Beyond homebrew and custom items, and Foundry dnd5e items, were imported as ADVENTURING_GEAR (Foundry shields as ARMOR) with no properties or damage, so an equipped imported weapon or shield never took a hand (D107, SHEET-8). Field shapes were checked against a real D&D Beyond character (74476867). The dnd5e Equipment effect and modifier builders moved to shared/authored and are used by the SRD corpus (output byte-identical, sha256 72a7281e…) and imports. Known limits: weapon-mastery properties are dropped; a versatile or thrown weapon with reach keeps the standard 5 ft range.

acs.text: A custom item imported from D&D Beyond or Foundry gets its real category (weapon, armor, shield, tool or gear) and its weapon properties, including two-handed and versatile.

An imported custom weapon keeps its damage dice, damage type, ability modifiers and magic bonus as a weapon attack; imported custom armor or a shield keeps its armor class, DEX rule and magic bonus; rarity is kept when the System knows it.
An imported Character with an equipped custom weapon or shield holds it in a hand, and an equipped custom armor is worn.

Resolve imported damage type, rarity, currency, speed and skill names to the System vocabulary during import preparation, so preview and commit agree on the payload and activation; an unknown damage type or armor vocabulary is reported as an import issue, not guessed.
Journey test: import a Character with the real equipped Astral Tear (+1 finesse shortsword) and a custom two-handed weapon and see them held in the main hand with their attacks.

features.title: Character Sheet
features.summary: The Character Sheet: projection, hit points, rolls, equipment, replay and the Speed fact.

pbis.title: View and edit a Character Sheet

acs.text: The personal Sheet browser journey covers HP, inspiration, conditions, inventory, currency, notes, rests, reload and Owl/Sailing Ship extras with strict diagnostics.
The Spell browser journey covers Learn, Prepare, Cast, reload, slot recovery, Unprepare and Forget within the one-second command limit.
Outside live play, Sheet commands write state, version and receipt atomically, and exact replay returns the current Sheet (ADR 0035).
proof: reworded, user-approved 2026-09-27 (ADR 0035): "outside live play" narrows the clause; the entries above still prove it

acs.text: The owner-only Sheet read ignores draft contents and evaluates current authorized sources.

pbis.title: Track hit points, resources and rests

acs.text: Personal and Campaign short and long rest preview and completion share current policy, fingerprints and caller-owned hit-die evidence.
One mutation persists HP, hit dice, exhaustion, slots and resources, companions, maximum-HP modifier removal, roll consumption, history and the receipt.
Rests delete only matching scalar-reduction effects, and rollback and exact replay perform no second deletion.

pbis.title: Roll dice with trusted results

acs.text: Personal, Campaign TABLE, private GM and Character-private rolls use current authority, Sheet mechanics and server-side unbiased randomness.
Roll evidence persists only in the caller's bounded private history or the TABLE conversation, and private rolls write nothing to the conversation.
Forged and foreign rolls are denied; history trims, replays, discards and clears; rest receipts consume rolls; failures roll back.

Player Campaign rolls default to the Table, with To GM and Just me options, and rolls that change Character state (such as short-rest hit dice) are always GM-visible: Table or To GM, never Just me (ADR 0034).

pbis.title: Characters hold items in their hands
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-10 by the product owner (D107); done 2026-10-11. Dev data migrated by local reset and reseed (backup local-validation/convex-reset/sheet-8-held-items.before.zip). Uses the hand slots and hand-occupancy function introduced by AUTHORING-17, so Characters and Creatures share one rule.

acs.text: Equipping a held item puts it in the main hand, then the off hand; each hand holds at most one item; a two-handed weapon takes the main hand and blocks the off hand; a shield is held in a hand, and a Character may hold two.
The player can swap the main-hand and off-hand items; emptying the main hand moves an off-hand weapon into it, while an off-hand shield stays where it is.
A shield adds to the Character's AC only while held in a hand, and only one shield counts.

pbis.title: GM loot tables on Scenes and Encounter creatures
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-10; rescoped by the product owner 2026-10-21. A loot table is a GM reference with exclusive roll ranges; the app never resolves a check against it. Not authored on creatures: a creature’s gear stays stats and gameplay. Giving an item to a Character from the table is in future-enhancements.

acs.text: A GM authors loot tables on a Scene and on a creature placed in an Encounter. Each table has a name, an optional check from the System’s skills, and exclusive roll ranges that may not overlap. Each range lists real catalog items (SRD or homebrew) with quantities, coins in the System’s denominations, and an optional note. Tables save and reopen, and overlapping ranges are refused with a named message.

In a live Session, the GM’s Loot panel lists the current Scene’s tables and the tables of defeated creatures, whose tokens show a loot marker. The GM enters a roll result and the matching range is highlighted. Players see none of it, and nothing is resolved or granted automatically.

pbis.title: One shared table screen for players in the same room
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-12 by the product owner. Replanned 2026-10-19 with the product owner (docs/handoffs/scene-5-plan.md) to a Foundry-style MVP: the GM grants Campaign-level control of other players’ Characters, and the controlling member opens the tabletop on the TV. No table role or projection. The old AC 5.3 (private information off the shared screen) is removed and documented as a limitation. Depends on VTT_UI-3.4 for per-Character senses.

acs.text: The GM can give a Campaign member control of other players’ Characters and take it back at any time; the owners keep control. A member moves a controlled Character’s token on the tabletop as its owner can, and in every Encounter they are one of its controllers.

A member who controls several Characters sees the Scene through one main Character’s senses, which they pick on the tabletop and which defaults to their own Character. Selecting a single token they control switches the view to that token’s senses; clearing or multi-selecting returns to the main Character. They never see what the viewed Character cannot see.

Every tabletop viewer can set the zoom by typing a percentage or stepping it, and their tabletop window keeps that zoom on that device across reloads, reconnects and view switches. The tabletop opens in a window sized to the screen and offers a Full screen button.

pbis.title: Auras, hidden hazards and traps

acs.text: Auras and traps execute against moving tokens, with their previews and privacy.
acs.note: Original PARTIAL: auras and traps execution is not in 8.2 criteria; movement and geometry facts are covered by V03/V07. 2026-10-14: auras are SPELLS-20; traps are made concrete by MOVE-3.2 to MOVE-3.6. Closed 2026-10-27 by MOVE-3.T6.

acs.text: The GM places a zone on a Scene through a GM zone tool that renders the same zone node map as authored content (shape, label, entry interactions and behaviors), so an environmental trap needs no trap-specific contract; it resolves like any placed zone, and GM undo removes it. Proved with an authoring-parity test: a GM-built pit and a GM-built caltrop field resolve the same as authored zones.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). Environmental traps exist only on the Scene; there is no trap subject or item category. A hazard is any ZONE with an entry interaction. Closed 2026-10-26 by MOVE-3.T1a, MOVE-3.T1b.

acs.text: A placed zone has an optional spot DC and an optional disarm DC, which the GM sets at placement or later by typing a flat number or the result of the placer's Stealth or Sleight of Hand roll. A zone without a spot DC is in plain sight. A concealed zone is drawn and listed only for the GM and the Characters that know of it, redacted per viewer on the server.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). Players lay their own hazards and roll on their sheet; the GM types the result. Per-viewer redaction follows the ATTACK-17.3 rule. Closed 2026-10-26 by MOVE-3.T2.

acs.text: A ZONE manifest can author camouflage: an optional concealment whose spot DC uses an existing DC method (for example the source's spell save DC), available in the zone node map; placing such a zone sets its spot DC automatically. Proved with an author-built camouflaged spell zone through the real form.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). SRD Spike Growth adopts it when SPELLS-4.2 converts it to core options. Closed 2026-10-26 by MOVE-3.T3.

acs.text: A campaign setting chooses how concealed zones are noticed: GM prompt (default) or Search only. With GM prompt, when a Character that does not know of a concealed zone first has it in sight and its passive Perception meets the spot DC, only the GM gets a quiet prompt to reveal it to that Character; players see nothing either way. There is no Search button: a player rolls from their sheet and the GM decides.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). Rejected: automatic reveal and player-facing passive roll requests, because either tells the table that something is there. Closed 2026-10-27 by MOVE-3.T4a, MOVE-3.T4b.

acs.text: A creature that does not know of a concealed zone gets no path warning and no Move carefully offer; entering it triggers it. The GM's path preview shows which creatures have not noticed it.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). Move carefully is Q2 (SPELLS-17). Closed 2026-10-27 by MOVE-3.T5.

acs.text: The GM can reveal a concealed zone to chosen Characters (after a Search roll or from the passive prompt) and can disarm a zone, which removes it; GM undo restores either. The disarm DC is shown only to the GM.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14 (decisions: hazards and traps). The player rolls the disarm check from their sheet. A botched disarm is the GM's call; on-demand triggering is a future enhancement. Closed 2026-10-27 by MOVE-3.T6.

pbis.title: Grapple and shove

acs.text: The Grapple basic action is offered only to a Character, or a Creature of a hand-bearing type, with a free hand. It replaces one attack of the Attack action against a creature within reach and no more than one size larger: the grappler's Athletics is contested by the target's choice of Athletics or Acrobatics (rolled by its controller), and a win applies Grappled owned by the grappler, with at most 2 creatures held at once through this action. With both hands holding weapons, the actor is prompted to stow one for free; a held shield cannot be stowed this way. Each creature held occupies a hand until the grapple ends.
acs.note: D105 slice C, D106 and D107. Refined 2026-10-10 into 7.1 and 7.3-7.8 (rul-9-rules-audit.md slice 2); the Grapple Limit stat was dropped 2026-10-10 for per-outcome held-at-once counts.

acs.text: A grappled creature can use its Action to escape with one of the grapple's authored checks, against its fixed escape DC or contested by the grappler's authored check; success ends the grapple.
acs.note: D105 slice B (fixed DC) done 2026-10-11: the Giant Toad journey offers the DC 13 escape, a d20 20 frees the Character (Grappled and Restrained removed) and a 1 keeps it; the room, Convex re-verification and drawer tests cover the rest. The contested escape is slice C.

acs.text: The grappler can release a grapple at any time with no action; a grapple ends when the grappler can't act, or when any movement leaves the grappled creature outside the grappler's reach.
acs.note: D105 slice D.

acs.text: A grappler that moves drags the creatures it grapples, at half speed unless each is two or more sizes smaller; dragged creatures provoke no opportunity attacks.
acs.note: D105 slice G.

acs.text: Shove replaces one attack of the Attack action against a creature within reach and no more than one size larger, with the same contest; on a win the shover knocks it prone or pushes it 5 feet away.
acs.note: D105 slice F.

acs.text: Forced movement is authored with a direction (away, toward, aside within the source's reach, or any) and an exact or up-to distance; away and toward follow the straight line from the source through the target (the mover chooses only how far, for an up-to distance), any lets the mover pick a legal unoccupied square, and it provokes no opportunity attacks. A homebrew Crusher feat (any direction, 5 feet, on a bludgeoning hit) proves the any-direction case.
acs.note: D105 slice E.

acs.text: SRD grapple riders author a Grappled outcome with their printed escape DC (Athletics or Acrobatics), printed size limit, "until this grapple ends" conditions and printed held-at-once count (the Kraken's tentacles 10; two claws, pincers or tentacles 2; otherwise 1), all editable in the Creature editor. Holds are counted per outcome, and a source-data test holds each rider to its stat block.
acs.note: D105 slice A. Swallow and other allowlisted riders stay with ATTACK-5. The live Giant Toad hit is the regression proof that a relationship's conditions on a Character bind to the receipt's active-effect CREATE (they failed the trace binding before). Since 2026-10-11 the room hit-rider test proves a Creature target ends Grappled and Restrained under one relationship effect; the pure rules test, stale since slice A, now asserts the effect's condition contributions.

acs.text: Grapple riders ("on hit, the target is grappled, escape DC N") and "grappled by this creature" targeting are authorable effects; the full Shambling Mound turn grapples a Medium or smaller target hit by both slams and then offers Engulf on it.
acs.note: D93. After ATTACK-11 (conditional slot).

acs.text: When a grapple's escape allows it (the Cloaker), another creature within reach of the grappled creature can use its Action to make the escape check and free it.
acs.note: D105. Registered 2026-10-11 in slice B: the SRD Cloaker authors `CREATURE_WITHIN_REACH` and no play path existed. Reuses the slice B escape command with the rescuer as the actor.

acs.text: A Barbarian rages in an Encounter: Rage is offered as a bonus action, spends a rage charge, and for its duration grants the level-scaled Rage damage bonus on Strength melee weapon attacks, resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and advantage on Strength checks and saving throws; while raging the Barbarian cannot cast spells or keep Concentration; Rage ends at its duration, by choice, or when the Barbarian is knocked unconscious (SRD; D113.3b); GM undo restores the charge. The feature is authored only from core authoring options (no CLOSED_RULE, no feature-specific kind or executor); an author-built equivalent made through the real authoring form publishes to the same structure and resolves identically.

pbis.title: Authored Multiattack with auto-sequence

acs.text: An author can author a Multiattack in the Creature editor as alternatives of attack slots (count, the actions that fill it, optional, comes first), with swaps and slot conditions (earlier slots in this action hit the same target; target size at most X), and publication refuses an invalid one.
acs.note: D93. After ATTACK-8 (shared slot model).

acs.text: All 142 SRD Multiattacks are authored as slot sets, and the stat-block audit refuses a description-only Multiattack.
acs.note: D93. Shambling Mound's conditional Engulf slot is authored here; Engulf itself is offered once ATTACK-7 lands.

acs.text: During a Multiattack only actions that fill a remaining slot of a still-feasible alternative are offered: a Brown Bear can't bite twice, a Drider's Bite swap is offered once, Frightful Presence only comes first, a Recharge that isn't ready isn't offered, and a conditional slot is offered only while its condition holds.

Auto-sequence: the GM's action drawer shows what is left of the Multiattack, preselects the only possible next attack and keeps the last target; the GM confirms each attack and can end the Multiattack early.
acs.note: D93. Assisted means assisted: nothing resolves without the controller's confirmation.

pbis.title: Weapons in hand during play
pbis.note: Registered 2026-10-10 by the product owner (D107). Builds on SHEET-8 and AUTHORING-17.

acs.text: The Attack action defaults to the main-hand weapon with full damage, and the bonus attack to the off-hand weapon, which adds no positive ability modifier to damage unless the actor has Two-Weapon Fighting; proficiency applies to both.

An attack draws its bound weapon into a free hand automatically. With no free hand, an actor holding creatures with the basic Grapple releases one to draw or attack, choosing which when it holds several.
A thrown weapon leaves its hand, and Disarm empties the disarmed item's hand; swapping weapons stays free.
acs.note: Swaps stay free per encounterWieldConflict.ts. The one free object interaction per turn is not tracked (future-enhancements.md).

With it off, the chosen ammunition still applies its bonuses and nothing is counted (D4 and its 2026-09-25 user override).

pbis.title: Area actions from a point (Fireball)

acs.text: The caster picks a point on the map for a point-origin area (sphere, cube, circle, cylinder); every creature inside it is caught, allies and the caster included; the caster and the GM see the list before it resolves, and only the GM can remove a creature from it. A point beyond range or out of sight is an overridable warning.
acs.note: rul-9-rules-audit.md slice 4, split 2026-10-10 into SPELLS-7 (point areas), SPELLS-13 (cones and lines), SPELLS-14 (cover), SPELLS-15 (area Legendary options), SPELLS-16 (caster spares creatures) and SPELLS-17 (placed zones, was 7.2 Caltrops). User ruling 2026-10-10: the app picks everyone in the area and the GM can adjust; a feature such as the Evocation wizard's Sculpt Spells lets the caster choose (SPELLS-16). The room computes the set, stores it with a currentness checksum and refuses if a token moved; the command carries a discriminated target (ACTOR or POINT), with no targetActorId alias. Built 2026-10-10 (D103). Out of sight (2026-10-10, D103): the caster's sight of the picked point is the D100 perception rules with the point as a subject with no conditions or effects (resolveEncounterPointSight), raising the overridable TARGET_OUT_OF_SIGHT beside TARGET_OUT_OF_RANGE; an undecided sight (a Creature's unmodeled free-text Senses) raises nothing. The room tests send the area action unacknowledged (refused with the warning, nothing opened or spent) and acknowledged (area opens) for range, a Blinded caster and a light-blocking wall. Web 2026-10-10 (5e4eec851, 0a1fd73cb, ec779091f): the action drawer picks the origin on the map or centers it on a token and previews who is caught; the decision drawer shows the caught list and per-role save groups, with GM-only removal and Legendary Resistance offers; Encounter history shows the issuer lines and GM-only lines. The live browser journey (apps/web/tests/live-backend/encounterArea.ts, runLocalConvexProof.ps1 -Proof area-browser) proves the pick, Escape cancel, GM removal, the player's own-save-only view, the commit's HP changes and the history.

acs.text: Every caught creature's save is asked at once, each by the creature's own roller; damage is rolled once and applies in full on a failed save and halved on a success, per target with its own defenses; the action commits once when the last save is in, and GM undo reverts every target.

acs.text: Concentration ends on incapacitation or death, and nonmagical-weapon defenses apply.
acs.note: D95, 2026-10-08. Done: direct actions, turn effects and Cleaving end Concentration with no check (nativeRoomConcentration, nativeRoomCleaving, nativeRoomTurnEffects, cleaving.test.ts, concentrationEnd.test.ts, encounterActorCannotAct.test.ts); nonmagical, silvered and adamantine defenses apply to direct and opportunity attacks (encounterDamageDefenses.test.ts, movementBasicActions.test.ts). GM UPDATE_ACTOR and Sheet edits done (slice C: endConcentrationAfterEdit; HP 0 or an incapacitating condition on a Creature, custom actor or Character in a running Run ends it in the edit's commit with one shared Sheet stream-version bump; MANUAL Runs, holders still able to act and Speed 0 alone end nothing).

acs.text: A Creature that holds Concentration makes a Concentration check when it takes damage that does not defeat it, and the commit succeeds.
acs.note: D95, 2026-10-08. A Creature or custom actor holder rolls the Constitution save like a Character: DC max(10, half damage), the Creature's save modifier (dnd5eConcentrationHolderSaves: the ability modifier plus the CR-based proficiency bonus of an authored save proficiency, pinned as the saveProficiencyBonuses rule fact so every Creature save uses it) and condition roll modes (D94). pbis.title: Concentrate on more than one spell

acs.text: An authored rule (on an item, Feature or other source) lets its holder keep a second Concentration when starting a new one, limited by authored conditions (such as a maximum spell level for both spells) and authored uses with a recovery (such as once per dawn); without it, or with no uses left, a new Concentration replaces the old one as today.
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-09 from the user's homebrew Ring of the Split Mind (very rare, attuned by a spellcaster): concentrating on a spell of 3rd level or lower, the wearer can cast a second 3rd-level-or-lower Concentration spell without losing the first, once per dawn. Design (user, 2026-10-09: generic, not built around the ring): Concentration capacity becomes a System stat (dnd5e default 1) held as a set of maintained states per actor; a capacity modifier joins the existing modifier pipeline from any source (equipped/attuned item, Feature, grant) with the existing predicates (WHILE_SOURCE_EQUIPPED etc.); the per-use gate is an authored predicate over the new and held spells (spell level) and the uses ride the existing limited-use/recovery model. No ring-specific code or kinds. After SPELLS-5.7, SPELLS-5.11 and SPELLS-8 (spell level comes from casting).

acs.text: With two Concentrations, damage asks for one Concentration save per spell, rolled in casting order, and each failure ends only its own spell and that spell's grants; an authored rule can add advantage or disadvantage to these saves under an authored condition (the ring: advantage while holding one spell; disadvantage on the second spell's save when the damage exceeds 10 + that spell's level).
acs.note: Registered with SPELLS-12.1. Per-spell saves are core engine behavior once capacity exceeds 1; the advantage/disadvantage are ordinary roll modifiers on Concentration saves with new authored predicates (held Concentration count, which Concentration the save is for, damage amount against a threshold). The ring's '10 + level of spell you are concentrating on' is authored data, so the GM's reading is what gets authored. D95 incapacitation ends both.

acs.text: An authored rule can apply an effect only while its holder keeps two Concentrations (the ring: vulnerability to psychic damage), and the effect ends when either Concentration ends; the caster can end either one by choice (SPELLS-5.11).
acs.note: Registered with SPELLS-12.1. The conditional effect is an ordinary modifier (damage vulnerability) gated by the held-Concentration-count predicate, evaluated where modifiers are read, not a timed grant. Journey: a Character with the authored ring holds Bless and Fly, takes damage, rolls two saves in order, loses one spell and keeps the other.

acs.note: Registered 2026-10-14 from the SPELLS-13 review: source data authors the breaths with SPECIAL range and no area shape (e.g. black-dragon-wyrmling.ts Acid Breath), so no SRD Creature can breathe through the area executor; the SPELLS-13 proofs use a synthetic Self cone action. pbis.title: Self-radius areas centered on the caster

acs.text: An area with Self range and a sphere, cylinder or circle shape ("each creature within 10 feet of it") is centered on the caster's space, catches every creature whose token overlaps it except the caster unless the text says so, and resolves as SPELLS-7 does.
proof: apps/session-worker/test/nativeRoomCasterCenteredAreaAction.test.ts (live room: caster-centered area, no aim, caster excluded)
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-14 from the SPELLS-13 review: SPELLS-13 builds cones, lines and Self cubes and still refuses Self sphere, cylinder and circle areas. Moving auras are SPELLS-20; outcomes that leave conditions stay refused until SPELLS-19. Token rotation is not tracked: 5e footprints are square, so it changes no catch. Merged 72193db49; D114 adopted (edge-of-space measure, D103 overlap, caster excluded).

pbis.title: Aiming a directed area on the map

acs.text: Pressing, dragging and releasing on the map aims a cone, line or Self cube and commits exactly the drawn origin and direction; a point picked for a directed area, or a direction for a point area, is refused with its own message; proved through the renderer gesture and the room refusals.

pbis.title: Frightened follows its source
origin: SPELLS-19.T2 escalation 2026-10-16: Frightened applies while present and its source is not tracked (D-limits at SPELLS-2)

acs.text: A Frightened condition applied by an action records the creature that frightened it, authored from core options (no Fear-specific kind). The frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls only while that source is within its line of sight, and a move that ends closer to the source is a soft-enforcement warning the GM can override (ADR 0034). A Frightened with no recorded source keeps its present always-on disadvantage. Proved for Fear, including GM undo.
origin: SPELLS-19.T2 escalation 2026-10-16; confirmed by the user 2026-10-16 (a move that ends closer warns, the GM can override)

acs.text: An effect can make a frightened creature flee its source (SRD Fear; Eyebite Panicked). It is authored from core options, not as a Fear-specific kind. At the start of the creature's turn its controller is told it must take the Dash action and move away from the source by the safest route. An action or move that does otherwise is a soft-enforcement warning with "Do it anyway", logged for the GM (ADR 0034). When the creature ends its turn without line of sight to the source, the app offers the authored saving throw (Wisdom for Fear). Success ends the effect for that creature only. Proved for Fear, with GM undo.
origin: Confirmed by the user 2026-10-16 (prompt plus warning with Do it anyway; automatic out-of-sight save)

The out-of-sight repeat save is proved by the two T1a tests in the same file.

An author can give a feature (Class, Feat, Creature trait) an always-on effect with no duration that ends on any condition from the existing End On list and returns after a long rest or a short rest. features.summary: What players, controllers and the GM can see in live and Campaign data.

pbis.title: Players see only redacted combat data

acs.text: The GM receives full data, Character controllers receive their decisions, other players receive redacted views, and hidden actors, targets and server snapshots are excluded.
Anonymous, outsider, departed and revoked users are refused, and ownership transfer changes the audience.
Every current producer uses the reviewed current-authority dispatcher.
Every command result and replay a player receives is the redacted player projection, and the room refuses anything else.

pbis.note: Done 2026-10-14 (merge of claude/eloquent-satoshi-e04d3f). The journey runs the real room with real SRD content: a GM walk raises a reaction decision, the sender answers or the GM voids it, and the retry replays what live sent; only fetch and dice are faked.

acs.text: A retried movement decision answer or GM void replays both the Scene receipt and the Encounter result its sender was sent live, each projected for the current viewer, not the Encounter result alone.
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-12 from the VTT_UI-3.4 review. Done 2026-10-14: #commitRoomGeometry stores [Scene message, Encounter message] as the receipt when a movement decision settles, and throws (rolling back) unless the command is a movement decision exactly when an Encounter result exists, so Scene commands keep their single-message receipt. The Encounter REPLAY sends the stored Scene receipt then re-presents the Encounter result per viewer (player answer, GM void, hidden-mover redaction, changed-payload refusal). docs/architecture/live-sessions.md documents the two-message receipt. Red/green logs in local-validation/reliability-3/.

pbis.title: Measuring a Scene length never crashes an Encounter read

acs.text: Encounter reads that measure Scene lengths (cleaving facts, movement reaction contacts, combat perception and its contributions) never throw: a Squares Scene measures each square as the System's 5 ft base square (D50 item 11), so every rule length measures correctly on it, and an authored length is bounded so it cannot overflow; proved by tests that fail before the fix.
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-13 from the VTT_UI-3.1 review. Ranges are length-only since the 3.1 merge, so the non-length throw is gone; lengthMeasurementInSceneUnits still throws for overflow and an uncalibrated SQUARES grid, and encounterCleavingFacts, encounterMovementReactionContacts, encounterCombatPerception and encounterCombatPerceptionContributions call it uncaught. Also covers the session-worker typecheck script failing `wrangler types --check` (worker-configuration.d.ts stale). Done by lane 3: a square is the System's 5 ft base square and a SQUARES grid's distancePerCell is always 1, so every Scene length is measurable; authored lengths are capped at AUTHORED_LENGTH_AMOUNT_MAX and Scene amounts at SCENE_LENGTH_AMOUNT_MAX, so overflow is unrepresentable; a sense range is DISTANCE or UNLIMITED with no long range or scaling; the session-worker types script generates from .dev.vars.example. Accepted 2026-10-13 by lane 1: lane 3 merged in 8dda19f80; post-merge builds, codegen, typechecks, root packages 2189/2190 (srd/import timeout flake only), session-worker 567/567, vtt and Sheet web unit 377/377 on the merged tree.

acs.text: A new Scene grid's default distance per cell is the System's base square in the chosen unit (5 ft, 1.524 m, 1 square), derived from SYSTEM_BASE_SQUARE_FEET and FEET_PER_SCENE_UNIT, and switching the unit converts it; proved by a Scene preparation test that fails first.
acs.note: Registered 2026-10-13 at the lane 3 merge review. CampaignScenePreparation seeds distancePerCell with SYSTEM_BASE_SQUARE_FEET for both FEET and METERS, so a Meters grid starts at 5 m per cell; feetInSceneUnit(SYSTEM_BASE_SQUARE_FEET, unit) gives the value for every unit and removes the SQUARES special case. Done 2026-10-13 (slice-reliability-4.md): a new Meters grid starts at 1.524 m; switching units converts the typed value (convertSceneDistance, exact via METERS_PER_FOOT, which also fixes 1.5240000000000002) and SQUARES forces 1. Red logs web-red-true.log and shared-red.log. Accepted by lane 1 on the merged tree: shared 9/9, web 8/8, worker 12/12, typecheck 19/19.

acs.note: Q3 answered (lane 1): the inner ring shows disposition, drawn and proved per disposition; control no longer changes the ring and "Yours" is in the description. Art presentation proved by CampaignVttPresentation TokenArtIsPresented. Selection wired (lane 3): with the Select tool, a press on any token selects it (control is not required), a press on the empty map clears it, and Focus in Scene controls selects that token; the selection is derived from the Scene so it ends when its token leaves. The Workshop Teal outline and the ", selected" description are proved by CampaignTabletopWindow SelectingATokenOutlinesIt; red `sel-red` (Stage wiring absent) and `sel-guard-red` (a press on a token the member cannot move cleared the selection). Accepted by lane 1 on 2026-10-12 (merged `d423a2d67`): disposition rings, art (TokenArtIsPresented), an outline distinct from the ring and halo (SelectionOutlineMarksOnlyTheSelectedToken), and selection journey SelectingATokenOutlinesIt.

acs.text: Conditions, Concentration and effects are presented as a segmented outer ring around the token's disposition border: one segment per active status, coloured by category (harmful condition, Concentration, beneficial effect, other), in model order, at most eight with the last marking overflow; hover, focus or selection lists every status by icon and name; the token is inset within its footprint so the outer ring never overlaps a neighbour; turn and reaction halos stay distinct from both rings (Q3).
acs.note: Implemented in vttTokenPresentation.model.ts and CampaignVttPresentation stories; not accepted. Integration-owner ruling 2026-10-12: harmful and beneficial come from a polarity derived in rules-runtime from each grant's modifiers relative to its holder (an all-beneficial grant is beneficial; an all-harmful grant is harmful; a mixed or neutral grant is other), never an authored flag. Conditions are harmful. The derived polarity is carried on the active grant listing. Built (D110): b5a55b5da. Presentation stories build from the real presentation model over Encounter data: ordering, overflow, reaction halo over current turn, defeated. Window journeys GmSeesTokenStatuses and PlayerSeesTokenStatusesWithoutGmHealth. Journey stays partial: 1.1 waits on token selection, 1.3 is held. Lane 3: Two rings (decision Q3): an outer segmented status ring (model order, at most 8 segments, the last marks overflow at 9+), inset inside the footprint, and a DOM status list on hover or focus. Proved against drawn output (segment count and category colours, overflow, inner and outer ring bounds of neighbouring 1x1 and large tokens) in the presentation and window stories; category hues and disposition ring colours pinned to literal hexes in the model tests; at least 2 units of clearance between the two rings on every side (red with the old inset 9: local-validation/lane3/logs/tight-red.log). The pending-frame hover fix is proved in the real storybook runner: with its render disabled, HoveringATokenRebuiltBeforeTheNextFrameReportsIt fails (local-validation/lane3/logs/rv-hover-red.log and tight-red.log). Status list paths proved: canvas hover lists a token's statuses and leaving hides them (window HoveringATokenOnTheCanvasListsItsStatuses), and keyboard focus on a token's Focus item in Scene controls (FocusingATokenListsEveryStatus). Mouse hover on that menu item and the selected token's list are proved since 99bc56fba. Completed 2026-10-13, awaiting integration-owner acceptance: b5a55b5da derives polarity in rules-runtime (listActiveGrantListings carries it on every listing) and the ring draws HARMFUL amber, BENEFICIAL lime 0x94d82d, CONCENTRATION and OTHER (neutral grants); red p12-red-rules and p12-red-web. 99bc56fba lists the selected token's statuses (red sel-status-red) and proves mouse hover on a Focus item. Accepted 2026-10-13 by the integration owner after review (fold contract carries typed modifier kinds and value domains; unknown codes fail at the fold; hidden sources show polarity; precedence story), merged in 3b684b7f8; post-merge worker 560, packages 1844, focused Convex 388, vtt unit 216 and stories 94 green, codegen unchanged.

acs.text: Light and map colour are rendered from the Scene: the ambient illumination sets the base (BRIGHT as authored, DIM visibly darkened, DARK black beyond light and senses); each light shows a full-brightness bright radius and a darkened dim radius, both tinted by its colour without washing out the map art; magical darkness stays black inside light except to senses that pierce it; obscurement draws as its own layer; the GM sees everything and can preview a chosen token's view.
proof: Closed by VTT_UI-3.T4 (m503); see each task's proof.
acs.note: Original PARTIAL: V03.5 covers visibility facts, not rendering. Refined 2026-10-12 by the product owner (map colour and darkvision); senses split into VTT_UI-3.4. Rules stay in rules-runtime and the Session Worker; apps/web only draws. Refined by the PO; D108 precedence. Rework of 6568f57eb: lights erase ambient darkness, DARK renders black, no vision wash, GM see-all and token-view preview, pixel-sampled proof against resolveSceneIlluminationAt. Lane 3: D108 precedence drawn as one darkness overlay whose alpha encodes the class (BRIGHT 0, DIM 0.5, ORDINARY and MAGICAL 1): ambient, then darkening zones, then lights erase within their radii clipped by walls, then magical darkness (zone or ambient) last. Light colour is a faint tint; obscurement its own layer; no vision wash, a player's map is black outside their tokens' sight. GM sees all at darkness alpha 0.6 (approved) and can preview one token's view. Lighting stories sample drawn overlay alpha at points and compare with resolveSceneIlluminationAt, including a torch in an ordinary darkness zone, magical darkness over a torch, a magically dark Scene, a wall blocking a light, and a closed versus an open door. The light tint is read from the drawn tint layer (light colour, alpha lightTintAlpha at most 0.2, one polygon per radius); visual-only zones draw at their own opacities (0.3 and 0.62, VisualZonesDrawAtTheirOwnOpacity; red with a fixed 0.5 in tight-red.log). A Player with no seeing token sees a black map. Through the Stage, the GM preview draws one sight polygon and stops on toggle-off or when the token leaves the Scene (window stories). Known behaviour (accepted by lane 1): the GM's chosen preview resumes if that token returns to the Scene. Awaiting lane 1 acceptance of the review fixes. The GM's Creature-token preview reads the Creature's stat-block senses since VTT_UI-5 (2026-10-14). Review fixes accepted by lane 1 and verified green in m503. Closed 2026-10-27 by VTT_UI-3.T4.

acs.text: A token's senses are rendered for the players who see through it: within darkvision range darkness shows as dim light in shades of grey and dim light shows as bright in full colour; beyond the range normal light rules apply; blindsight and tremorsense reveal within range regardless of light and truesight sees through magical darkness; the view draws the senses of one token at a time: the single selected token, otherwise the viewer's main Character (Q6, SCENE-5).
acs.note: Regression proof updated 2026-10-13 after the RELIABILITY-4 rulings: a sense range is never null; an UNLIMITED sense stays unlimited and shows on its token whatever the grid (vtt-scene.test.ts › presents an unlimited sense on the token whatever the grid can measure; length-measurement.test.ts; encounterCombatPerceptionSquaresScene.test.ts › keeps an unlimited pinned sense unlimited). Accepted 2026-10-13 by lane 1: lane 3 merged in 8dda19f80; post-merge builds, codegen, typechecks, root packages 2189/2190 (srd/import timeout flake only), session-worker 567/567, vtt and Sheet web unit 377/377 on the merged tree. Regression found 2026-10-13 (RELIABILITY-4 review): a Character sense with a null pinned range (unlimited in combat perception) was dropped from the token. Fixed red first: deriveCharacterSceneVision and resolveSceneCharacterVision keep it with range null, SceneTokenSense.range is nullable, and the renderer gives it an infinite reach, so it sees its whole line of sight (actorSenses.test.ts, vtt-scene.test.ts, vttSceneRenderer.model.test.ts; red logs local-validation/lane3/logs/red-root.log and red-web.log). Split from VTT_UI-3.2 on 2026-10-12 (product owner: a dwarf with darkvision in a cave sees grey within 60 ft and black beyond). Covers Character senses and authored token sight; Creature senses are VTT_UI-5. Implemented 2026-10-12 in e343e21a1 (A: senses on SceneToken, snapshot and delta redaction by ADR 0034 control) and 20b01c2c2 (B: renderer), awaiting integration-owner acceptance. Audit fixes 2026-10-12: 55c7547fd, 1e9d099e1, c201d2513 (exact retries replay the sender's projected receipt), bd5ce33b1, 3f037b60f and 2f0ea3811 (senses are never persisted: the stored Token schema requires empty senses, so definition appends and checkpoints both reject them), 794aca484 and 229749488 (drawn sight is the shared visibility polygon, with authored ranges converted to map pixels as server fog does), 32c2a55ab (every Scene receipt is the message the sender was sent), 9e54f0a7e (Scene definition batch replay proof restored; stored-senses refine reports path senses), 4bc4ee298 (bound senses withheld after a Character reassignment; visible-mover receipt replays as sent), 23f310ea6 (room seeding cancels its redundant scheduled Content Snapshot builds, replacing the real-clock wait of e8a3f415c). The movement decision replay that omits the Scene receipt is RELIABILITY-3. Vision is authored only; every seeing token sees along its line of sight clamped to its authored range, and within that the light and the view token's senses decide what shows. Truesight keeps DIM as DIM. Blindsight clears every darkness class within range and line of sight. Tremorsense treats every token as on the ground (the Scene has no elevation data) and reveals tokens through walls without changing the map. Tokens in darkness that no sense reaches are concealed; the view token and the Player's own tokens always show. The monster trait (imp, devils: magical darkness doesn't impede their darkvision) is darkvision-based and lands with VTT_UI-5 stat-block senses. Depends on lane 3's ruling 3 (no null sense range). pbis.title: Alpha testers have a play guide for the live table

acs.text: A plain-language guide with Player and GM sections explains every live-table flow an alpha tester meets: joining a Session, Scenes, tokens and movement, Manual versus Assisted Encounters, initiative, the turn stages (Recharge, death saves, start-of-turn effects), attacks, saves, spells and reactions, Public and Private GM rolls and their reveals, the auto-roll preference, and what can and cannot be undone.
acs.note: Written once the VTT behavior freezes before alpha, so it describes shipped behavior rather than plans. Source each rule from phase-08-2-decisions.md and the ADRs.

acs.text: The guide lists the known gaps testers will hit and tells them how to send feedback and what to include (Campaign, Scene, round, what they expected and what happened).
A walkthrough of the release candidate confirms every statement in the guide matches the build before alpha invites go out.

pbis.title: Review data for the owner's UI review

acs.text: A re-runnable local script builds named review Campaigns with members, Scenes with tokens and Encounters that cover the shipped play surfaces (a party of Characters, SRD Creatures, point and directed areas, spells and slots, conditions, Concentration, reactions, initiative and roll cards), through the product's own commands, against the local Docker Convex backend only; running it again after a reset rebuilds the same data.
acs.note: User ruling 2026-10-14: the owner reviews the UI locally before staging, using test Campaigns, Scenes and Encounters. The final local lifecycle (validatePreStagingLocal.mjs) resets local Convex first, so review data is a scripted seed run after RELEASE-2, not hand-kept data.

acs.text: The owner reviews the UI on the review data and signs off before staging promotion; findings are fixed or registered.
acs.note: Gate between RELEASE-2 (final local lifecycle) and RELEASE-3 (staging).
